los.text: Perform a neurological examination of the upper limbs with a structured and systematic approach
los.html:
• Order: inspection, tone, power, reflexes, coordination, sensation (compare sides).
StepDetail
InspectionWasting, fasciculation, tremor, scars, posture; pronator drift (arms out, palms up, eyes closed: UMN weakness drifts down and pronates)
ToneRotate the wrist and flex/extend the elbow: spasticity (clasp-knife, UMN), rigidity (cogwheel/lead pipe, Parkinson's), reduced (LMN)
Power (MRC 0–5)
  • Shoulder abduction (C5)
  • Elbow flexion (C5/6)
  • Elbow extension (C7)
  • Wrist extension (C6/7)
  • Finger extension (C7)
  • Finger flexion (C8)
  • Finger abduction (T1)
  • Thumb abduction (median, T1)
ReflexesBiceps (C5/6), supinator (C5/6), triceps (C7); reinforcement (clench teeth); Hoffmann's sign
CoordinationFinger–nose test (intention tremor, past-pointing), dysdiadochokinesia
Sensation
  • Light touch and pinprick by dermatome (C5 lateral arm, C6 thumb, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger, T1 medial forearm)
  • Vibration and proprioception (start distally)
PatternSigns
UMNIncreased tone, pyramidal weakness, brisk reflexes, no wasting
LMNWasting, fasciculation, reduced tone, reduced/absent reflexes

los.text: Perform a competent gastrointestinal examination with increased confidence.
los.html:
• Same structure as week 105, but faster and more fluent: inspection, hands, face, neck, abdomen (palpate, percuss, auscultate), and the finishing steps.
Focus for "increased confidence"
Smooth, systematic order without notes
Commentary to the examiner while examining (if asked)
Watching the patient's face throughout
Correct technique for liver (from RIF, with inspiration) and spleen (from RIF towards left costal margin; tip the patient right)
Shifting dullness: percuss to dullness in the flank, roll the patient, wait 30 s, re-percuss

los.text: Interpret basic clinical signs identified during a gastrointestinal examination.
los.html:
SignSuggests
JaundiceLiver disease, biliary obstruction, haemolysis
Spider naevi, palmar erythema, gynaecomastia, Dupuytren'sChronic liver disease
AsterixisHepatic encephalopathy (also CO₂ retention, uraemia)
ClubbingIBD, cirrhosis, coeliac disease
Koilonychia, pallorIron deficiency anaemia
HepatomegalyCongestion, fatty liver, malignancy
SplenomegalyPortal hypertension, haematological disease, infection
Ascites (shifting dullness)Cirrhosis, malignancy, heart failure
Caput medusaePortal hypertension
Murphy's signAcute cholecystitis
Ballotable kidneyPolycystic kidneys, renal tumour
Expansile massAAA

los.text: Explain simple medical concepts to patients using appropriate language and empathetic communication.
los.html:
TechniqueExample
Find out what they know first"What do you understand about your condition so far?"
Chunk and checkSmall pieces, then "Does that make sense so far?"
Plain language"Your blood sugar is too high" not "hyperglycaemia"
Analogies and drawingsArteries "furred up like a pipe"
Teach-back"Can you tell me in your own words what we discussed?"
EmpathyAcknowledge feelings and worries
Written information / leafletsBack up what you said
  • Avoid: jargon, information overload, false reassurance.
